issues.description: Metadata/PR docs promise PASS/FAIL but code emits a third MANUAL state for GKE
issues.detail: Metadata.json and the PR description specify a two-valued outcome (PASS for single NIC, FAIL for multiple), but the implementation introduces MANUAL for gke-* instances. The contract and code disagree. Either document MANUAL in metadata as part of the contract or move GKE handling to an allowlist/mute convention.

issues.description: GKE detection by name-prefix is a leaky, spoofable heuristic
issues.detail: Using `name.startswith("gke-")` to identify GKE-managed nodes is a string-match special case where authoritative signals exist (the `goog-gke-node` label or MIG membership). Any user-named instance can spoof a MANUAL pass. Add an `is_gke_managed` derived attribute on the Instance model and have the check consume that boolean instead.

issues.description: Check name, directory, and CHANGELOG drift from PR title and stated intent
issues.detail: The PR title and changelog describe detecting VMs with multiple NICs, but the CheckID, directory, files, and class are all `compute_instance_single_network_interface`. Pick one predicate and align CheckID, paths, class name, and changelog so the name matches the semantics and future greps work.

issues.description: Zero-NIC branch silently PASSes without a test and violates the stated postcondition
issues.detail: When `interface_count == 0`, the check returns PASS with an informational message. The PASS contract is "single network interface," so zero violates it, and no test covers this path. Either treat zero as MANUAL/INFO with an explicit decision or document/assert it as impossible per the GCP API.

issues.description: Mutable default `network_interfaces: list[NetworkInterface] = []` on the Instance model
issues.detail: Pydantic v1 happens to copy this safely, but the idiomatic and invariant-preserving form is `Field(default_factory=list)`. Match the surrounding codebase style and make per-instance ownership explicit to avoid aliasing risk on migration or subclassing.

synthesis.summary: The panel converges on three substantive problems: a contract mismatch where metadata documents only PASS/FAIL but the code emits a third MANUAL state for GKE, a leaky GKE detection heuristic that sniffs the `gke-` name prefix instead of using the authoritative `goog-gke-node` label or MIG membership, and persistent naming drift between PR title, CheckID, directory, and CHANGELOG. Secondary concerns include a silently-PASSing zero-NIC branch with no test coverage and a mutable default list on the Instance Pydantic model. The check is functional and tested on happy paths but needs its contract reconciled and the GKE signal moved into the service layer as a derived attribute before it should land.
